coverage: FactStamp entity-door coverage — what we verify, what we do NOT, and what it costs

jurisdictions.ownership_note: Beneficial owners are not public. The beneficial-owner API is restricted to banks, authorities and named civil-society bodies; we do not read it.
verifiable: company identity: name, organisation number, legal form
registered address and registration date
status flags straight from the register: VAT register, bankruptcy, winding-up, compulsory dissolution
industry code and employee count
corporate group structure: the parent and the chain of a registered group
not_verifiable: beneficial owners (closed)
the people behind the company (the roles surfaces are not read by this slice)
any personal identity number (never requested, never stored)

registers.name: Registered notifications (Finnish Trade Register, since 7 Nov 2014)

jurisdictions.ownership_note: Beneficial owners are not public, and the KRS open API masks the personal names of natural persons by law. We read the mask and say so; we do not read any owner register.
verifiable: entity identity — BY KRS NUMBER ONLY: name, legal form, NIP, REGON when present

the court that made the last entry

jurisdictions.ownership_note: Beneficial-owner data is no longer published as open data at all — the e-Business Register stopped it on 10 July 2026. The officer, board and shareholder files carry natural persons' names (personal data under the GDPR) and are NOT read. The basic-details file we DO read carries no officers or owners; it does include sole traders (FIE), whose registered name is the person's own name.

registers.name: e-Business Register open data — basic details (ettevotja_rekvisiidid__lihtandmed)

verifiable: company identity: the registry code (eight digits, with the register's own check digit), the name and the legal form and subtype
the VAT (KMKR) number, when the company is registered for VAT
registry status straight from the file (registered / in liquidation / bankrupt), as the register publishes it
first-entry date
the registered address (street, settlement unit, postcode, and the address system's normalised full address)
sole traders (FIE) too, as the register publishes them — held exactly as published
not_verifiable: officers, board members and shareholders — the register's officer and shareholder files carry natural persons' names (personal data) and are NOT read
beneficial owners — no longer published as open data (since 10 July 2026)
personal identity numbers (isikukood) — absent from the open data since 1 November 2024, and never requested or stored
annual-report figures and the commercial-pledge / order files — separate datasets this slice does not read
live freshness — the file is a DAILY bulk snapshot compiled by the register, so an answer states the file's own date, not a live read

price.fx_basis: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates

jurisdictions.ownership_note: Beneficial owners are not public. The register publishes the legal representative (whose NAME we read) and that person's identity document type and number (which we do NOT read or carry). Directors beyond the representative, shareholders and owners are not published.
verifiable: company identity: the NIT (with its check digit), the registered name and the matrícula (registration number)
the chamber of commerce that administers the registration
the register's own registration status (e.g. ACTIVA / CANCELADA)
the society type and the legal-organisation form
the primary and secondary CIIU economic-activity codes
the registration and last-renewal dates
the legal representative's NAME (the person who legally represents the entity)
not_verifiable: the legal representative's identity document type and number — present in the source; deliberately NOT read or carried

directors beyond the legal representative, shareholders and beneficial owners — not published in this dataset
financial statements — not published in this dataset
a bare 9-10 digit string as a NIT — a NIT is read only with its check digit (e.g. 900925798-3)

ownership_summary: Ownership data — who ultimately owns or controls a company — is CLOSED in nearly every country we cover. We can honestly verify that a company exists, who runs it (where the register publishes it), and its status; in most of Europe we cannot yet verify who ultimately owns it. Each jurisdiction below says which side of that line it is on.

charging.note: The live charging rail is UNCHANGED: the widened entity door settles at US$0.10 and the figure door at US$0.05, on the x402 and prepaid-pack rails. The local-currency figures on this surface are DISPLAYED pricing only.
charging.how_local_charging_would_slot_in: Per-jurisdiction pricing would slot in WITHOUT touching the live amount by adding a local-price entry keyed by the query's jurisdiction alongside the existing US dollar amount: the door would look up a dated local price (the same value shown here), quote it, and derive the USDC amount the rail settles from the dated FX rate, exactly as the entity FILE door already derives its amount from a pence rung. The US$0.10 amount stays the source of truth until Dan decides otherwise; nothing here changes what settles today.
